Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Summit Power Generation Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Summit Power Generation Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Jennifer Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jennifer Hale.

Jennifer Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
1. Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
2. Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
3. Effective cost management.
4. Progress on our infrastructure investments.
5. Successful integration of Buckeye Solar.
6. Advancement of our Net-Zero 2040 program.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects. Starting with our strong operational performance, we navigated significant weather challenges effectively. Then, our renewables portfolio saw meaningful expansion. Cost management kept us ahead of peers, infrastructure upgrades enhanced reliability, Buckeye Solar is now fully ramped, and our sustainability efforts are accelerating. Our team will expand on these throughout the call.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thornton to discuss the financials.

Michael Thornton: Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024 quarter, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.52 and revenue of $2.95 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.1 billion, primarily focused on renewables development, battery storage deployments, and grid resilience enhancements. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate adjusted EPS growth of 8% to 10% for full-year 2025, supported by rate base expansion and merchant market tailwinds.

One of the most telling indicators of our financial health in this regulated sector is our authorized versus earned return on equity analysis. This metric serves as a key benchmark, linking our regulatory allowances with shareholder returns. It shows how well we're converting investments in transitioning from coal to gas, scaling renewables, and building grid resilience into permitted earnings via rate base structures.

Our authorized ROE is established by regulators such as state public utility commissions in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky, along with FERC for our wholesale operations in MISO and PJM. These are set using methods like discounted cash flow, CAPM, and constant growth models, typically ranging from 9.5% to 10.75% following recent proceedings amid higher risk-free rates and equity premiums. Earned ROE is our actual realized return, computed as net income to common shareholders over average common equity on a trailing 12-month basis.

Looking at the five-year trend, in 2020 we had an authorized ROE of 10.25% against earned of 9.85%, a -40 bps gap due to COVID-impacted operations and maintenance deferrals. In 2021, authorized stayed at 10.25% with earned at 10.05%, narrowed by production tax credit and investment tax credit benefits from initial wind projects. 2022 saw authorized rise to 10.50% but earned at 9.95%, gapped by supply chain issues on combined-cycle conversions. 2023 authorized was 10.25% versus earned 9.60%, influenced by natural gas price swings despite hedging. For Q3 2024 year-to-date, authorized is 10.20% with earned at 9.75%, closing the gap to -45 bps thanks to better allowance for funds used during construction offset by weather adjustments.

Blended authorized ROE for Q3 stands at 10.20%, down 5 bps year-over-year, reflecting the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission's decision capping at 10.0%, tied to lower Treasury yields around 4.2%. FERC maintained 10.3% for our 2.4 GW wholesale assets in MISO South, aided by risk adders for battery storage positions.

Earned ROE rose to 9.75% trailing 12 months, up 15 bps from Q2, narrowing from -65 bps in late 2023. This modest under-earning is deliberate, as we prioritize rate base growth ahead of peers like Duke Energy and Ameren.

By region: In Ohio, representing 45% of rate base, authorized 10.0% versus earned 9.3%, gap widened by delayed recovery on our 800 MW Buckeye Solar at 75% commercial operations amid long interconnection queues. Indiana, 30% of rate base, authorized and earned closest at 10.0% and 9.8%, boosted by AFUDC on the 1.2 GW Lawrenceburg combined-cycle gas turbine conversion nearing completion, with gas at $2.85 per MMBtu and 90% hedged. Kentucky, 15%, authorized 10.5% earned 10.1%, driven by coal divestitures redirecting funds to 400 MWh battery pilots with our 1.1 GW wind assets. Wholesale MISO-PJM, 10%, FERC 10.3% earned 10.0%, supported by PJM capacity auctions at $270 per MW-day offsetting softer MISO pricing.

Variance drivers include 8.2% rate base growth to $18.5 billion from $1.2 billion capex, 60% in renewables and storage under IRA credits, generating AFUDC at around 5.8%. Opex down 4% to $1.85 per kW through drone predictive maintenance with GE Vernova's tools and AI dispatch, saving $25 million in outages. Regulatory sharing in multi-year plans lets us keep 50% of over-earnings, though FERC inquiries pose risks. Wholesale prices up 12% to $42 per MWh.

Strategically, we're narrowing the gap with $500 million in distributed energy resource management systems and synchrophasors for FERC compliance, renewables to 40% unforced capacity by 2027 with IRA support, and a Q1 2025 Indiana rider seeking 10.4% ROE. Our -45 bps gap fuels 7% equity earnings growth, with ROIC at 8.9%, better than peers' wider spreads. We expect stability at 10.2-10.4% authorized, earned converging soon.

Turning to earnings guidance, we've raised our outlook reflecting strong demand from data centers in MISO and PJM, new solar-storage hybrids, and IRA benefits, tempered by gas prices and residential normalization.

For Q4 2024, we project revenues of $2.70 billion to $2.80 billion, up 10-14% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS at $1.60 to $1.70, ahead of consensus. This assumes temperatures 5% above normal for cooling demand. Merchant fleet, 65% of 28 GW capacity, captures higher spark spreads with gas at $3.20-$3.50 per MMBtu. In MISO where we have 4.5 GW peakers and 1.2 GW storage, prices could hit $45-$50 per MWh. Regulated revenues grow 7% on capex, though O&M up slightly from supply chains.

Full-year 2024: Revenues $11.0 billion to $11.3 billion, up 11-15%; adjusted EPS $5.80 to $6.00, 12% growth at midpoint. AFFO for renewables $3.55-$3.70. Uplift from 3.5% demand growth, data center PPAs at 1.2 GW, coal divestiture proceeds for CCUS, 1.1 GW renewables additions shifting to 45% carbon-free. Hedged 75% gas at $3.10, nuclear at 95% factor. Regionally, MISO EBITDA up 18% on scarcity, PJM capacity at $270/MW-day, Southeast ROE 10.2%. 2025 capex $2.5 billion, 60% clean tech, FCF $1.9-$2.1 billion for dividends and buybacks.

On regulatory lag, a persistent challenge stems from the delay between capex outlays for hardening, renewables, and load growth versus rate recovery by commissions. For our 15 GW regulated fleet and lines in PJM-MISO, lag averaged 12-18 months, costing $325 million in 2023 or 45 bps on EPS from $2.8 billion capex, only 65% into rates. Compounded by inflation and debt costs at 5.1%.

Regionally, PJM states allow 75% CWIP minimizing lag; MISO slower on clean mandates. Mitigations: Advanced rate cases for $1.1 billion, trackers recovering 95% variables, multi-year plans embedding AFUDC, capex efficiencies via GridOS saving $120 million, demand response for capacity credits, securitization and green bonds. Aiming for 6-9 month lag by 2026, supporting 7-9% EPS growth.

Grid modernization is another high-return area. We've invested $650 million over 24 months, 18% of rate base adds, including AMI rollout to 85% of 2.8 million customers in Ohio-Indiana-Kentucky via Itron meters, cutting SAIDI 22% to 93 minutes, saving $45 million. ADMS with GE GridOS integrates SCADA, FLISR preventing 15,000 interruptions, CAIDI down 18%. 12,000 IoT sensors forecast failures at 92% accuracy.

In Indiana hydro-heavy areas, DERMS integrates 450 MW solar-wind at 98% accuracy. Kentucky EV growth supports TOU and VPPs earning $28 million. IIJA grants $180 million for HVDC, ABB pilots, Dragos cybersecurity. $1.2 billion next five years for 100% AMI, $120 million annual O&M savings, 50 bps ROE boost, NPS to 78.

These efforts de-risk renewables to 40% by 2030, supporting EPS.

Thank you. Now over to Sarah for operations.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Michael. Let me provide an update on the operational front, including our storm response. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to the implementation of predictive maintenance using AI and drones. This has resulted in a 12% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 25%.

Specifically on storm response from Hurricane Elara, which hit as a Category 3 on September 12th with 120 mph winds and 20 inches of rain in Kentucky and Indiana areas. Our Storm Central center used SCADA, GIS, and AI from Siemens for predictions. Peak outages hit 2.8 million customers, 35% of load, from downed lines and 12,000 poles.

We deployed 4,500 personnel, including mutual aid from Duke and others, restoring critical infrastructure in 6-12 hours, 92% customers in 48 hours, full in 6 days—beating benchmarks, limiting YTD SAIDI impact.

Recovery costs $285 million ($165M opex, $120M capex), $210M recoverable via insurance, deferrals, riders at 10.35% ROE, net $0.04 EPS hit. Used drones/LiDAR for fast inspections, 50,000 reclosers, temporary BESS, vegetation clearing, 8,500 FRP poles, 150 miles undergrounded. Kentucky saw surge corrosion, Carolinas-like wind shear.

Storms up 20% per decade; we've cut unit costs to $95/customer vs. peers. Filing $1.2B hardening rider for undergrounding, microgrids, AMI to 95%, enhancing ROE.

Thank you.

David Patel: Thank you, Sarah. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration battery storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the PJM and MISO markets.

On progress against initiatives, our clean energy transition is ahead: 1.2 GW renewables YTD, including 450 MW Solar Ridge with First Solar bifacials at 28.5% efficiency, total renewables 8.7 GW or 42% mix, up 22%. Wind: 300 MW Prairie Winds III with GE 3.8 MW turbines at 45% capacity factor.

BESS: 850 MWh deployed, 400 MWh PJM with Tesla Megapacks/AI, $45M ancillary revenue. Queue 4.2 GW, 1.8 GW building, IRA 50% ITC.

ERCOT growth: 2.5 GW data center PPAs at $65/MWh. PJM VPPs 250 MW, $18M capacity. CAISO limited, LCFS benefits.

Decarbonization: Toward 70% carbon-free 2030, net-zero 2045. CCUS FEED on 1,200 MW gas at Rockport, 90% capture, 45Q $150/ton. H2 blending 20%, nuclear uprates 50 MW.

Grid resilience: $450M AMI to 85%, peak shave 8%, microgrids post-storms. Zero-trust cyber.

Demand: 15-20% CAGR in territories from data centers. Target 15 GW clean by 2030, funded 40% earnings, 30% green bonds at 4.75%, 30% tax equity. ROE +150 bps/year.

Risks mitigated, IRA $250M YTD. Executing for outsized returns.

Thank you.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed advanced OT threat detection from Dragos to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

Thank you, Michael, Sarah, David, and Lisa. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for further expansion of the renewable portfolio?

Jennifer Hale: Certainly. We're accelerating with 1.2 GW online YTD, pushing renewables to 42% of our mix, and a 4.2 GW BESS queue. Data center PPAs in PJM and MISO at premium rates, CCUS and hydrogen pilots for hard-to-abate assets, targeting 15 GW clean capacity by 2030 to meet electrification demand.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for closing the ROE gap next year?

Michael Thornton: Our earned ROE improved to 9.75%, -45 bps gap, through capex momentum, opex cuts, and regulatory mechanisms. With rate filings and in-service flows from Buckeye Solar and Lawrenceburg CCCT, we see convergence to authorized 10.2-10.4%, supporting 7-9% EPS growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How are you mitigating risks related to regulatory lag?

Sarah Kline: We're proactive with advanced rate cases for CWIP recovery, trackers for 95% passthrough, multi-year plans, and efficiency gains from GridOS and demand response. Securitization and PBR advocacy will compress lag to 6-9 months, minimizing EPS impact amid capex surge.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Jennifer Hale for closing remarks.

Jennifer Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Summit Power Generation Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Summit Power Generation Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
